title: Every request accounted for
subtitle: The tool-discovery model's fleet daemon has a nine-point service contract: 512 requests offered to 64 clients with a queue of sixteen gave 244 answered, 268 refused with a typed reason and none dropped, and a shutdown that answered every request in flight
technologies: Capacity engineering, backpressure and load testing

refused with a typed busy reason

lede: The tool-discovery model answers one question, which tool does this request need, for every agent in my estate, and it does so from a GPU it shares with a larger serving model. A router beside a production model tells how it fits in the memory it is allowed. This is how it serves: a daemon whose contract says what happens to every request it is offered, including the ones it refuses. The serial daemon runs one thread per connection over a Unix socket and holds the engine behind a single mutex. Decode is batch-one there, so the mutex is the queue and nothing more is needed.
quote: A refusal before bind means no client ever saw a half-ready service.
evidence: Service contracts for inference daemons: a nine-point contract under which 512 requests offered by 64 clients to a queue of sixteen gave 244 answered and 268 refused with a typed reason.
Backpressure and load shedding: a bounded queue in which every refusal carries a typed busy reason and no request is dropped.
Graceful shutdown: 8 of 8 requests in flight answered when the daemon was terminated.
Continuous batching: one engine thread stepping rows from every sequence in flight, each in its own paged cache, so a short answer never waits for a long one.
MCP server design: the daemon reachable as a standard tool-protocol server over standard input and over streamable HTTP with TLS.
author: Corey James
